analysis.title: Earnings Season Pulse: Earnings hold up but AI optimism is fracturing
key_insights: Global 3Q26 earnings were better than feared last week, with high beat rates across US health care, industrials and financials, alongside strength in European technology and telecom.
AI supply chain results showed spending continuing to accelerate. Microsoft Azure grew 48% vs 44% consensus, and Amazon AWS grew 39% to $46bn.
Tokyo Electron guided to nearly 90% operating-profit growth. SK Hynix reported a sevenfold profit increase, with HBM capacity sold out through 2029.
Investors are demanding proof that AI spending generates returns. Amazon fell 5.9% after quarterly capex reached $77bn, and Alphabet dropped more than 7% on weaker advertising and services revenue.
Samsung declined 4% despite record profits, as investors viewed rising capex without higher shareholder returns as defensive.
Caterpillar fell 9.3% despite beating estimates, which SG reads as AI exposure alone no longer being enough to support premium valuations.
Semiconductors are running at two speeds. HBM and semiconductor equipment are the strongest segments, while NAND and legacy computing are weakening.
Kioxia's operating-profit guidance was roughly 15% below consensus. Intel guided 4Q revenue to $15-16bn vs $17bn expected, triggering a 27% pre-market decline.
China memory maker CXMT's sequential growth slowed to 19% from 90% in 2Q26, and the stock has lost 8% since.
China remains the main earnings risk for global autos. Volkswagen's Chinese joint ventures swung from a EUR744m profit to a EUR113m loss.
Mercedes cut its margin guidance to 2-3% from as much as 5%, and Audi lowered its operating-margin forecast to 3-5%.

Chinese automakers are also under pressure. BYD missed estimates, Great Wall Motor net income fell 41%, and Geely shares fell despite a 26% rise in net income as investors focused on European trade barriers.
Of 1,663 global companies with consensus, 964 have reported: 452 (27%) above consensus, 216 (13%) in line, 296 (18%) below, and 699 (42%) still to report.
S&P 500 coverage: 300 of 499 companies have reported EPS. STOXX 600: 170 of 335 have reported EPS. CSI 300 is nearly complete at 209 of 210.
